name: pey.visualization
description: Data visualization as a rendering service over a swappable chart renderer (Observable Plot today, hidden behind an internal adapter): create, update and remove independent charts in host-provided containers; the host owns the data and its meaning, the plugin owns the drawing

provides.name: pey.visualization.service
provides.description: Chart rendering for data the host has already prepared. The plugin receives data and display settings, draws the chart, and offers the agreed display interactions; it never fetches, stores, interprets or computes anything of business meaning — only the computations a chart type itself needs (binning, quantiles, stacking, scales). The chart library stays behind an internal renderer adapter and never leaks into this surface. Events carry chart/series identity, never raw payloads beyond the clicked datum.

methods.name: create
methods.description: Creates one independent chart in a host-provided container (an element or a CSS selector, resolved once) and returns its unique id. Data and display options are validated first: an unknown chart type, invalid container, invalid options or invalid data fail with their own codes; empty data is not an error — the chart renders an empty state.

params.name: input
params.type: { container: Element | string, type: string, data: object, options?: object }

methods.name: update
methods.description: Re-renders an existing chart with new data, new options or both. Options given alone keep the previous data; data given alone keep the previous options — unless the caller overrides them. Re-rendering redraws the whole chart; no partial transitions are promised.

params.name: id
params.type: string — the chart id from create

params.name: input
params.type: { data?: object, options?: object } — at least one of the two

methods.name: remove
methods.description: Removes a chart completely: its display is taken off the page, every resource the plugin kept for it is freed, and other charts continue untouched. An unknown id fails with its own code.

params.name: id
params.type: string — the chart id from create

events.name: visualization:click
events.description: The user clicked a chart part the renderer supports selecting. Identifies the chart, the series and the clicked datum when available.

events.name: visualization:series-toggled
events.description: The user switched a data series on or off through the chart legend.
